subject: convoyHauler
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: armoured convoy hauler guarding a sealed cargo pod.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.

spec.name: Convoy Hauler Mk-IV
spec.description: A low-poly cyberpunk armoured six-wheel convoy hauler with a wedge cab, gun turret and a sealed glowing cargo pod on its back.
spec.layout: A long, low armoured truck facing +Z. Front: a wedge-nosed cab with a slanted cyan visor, bull bar and headlights, a ram plate at the very front. Middle: a flat chassis deck on three axles (six large chunky wheels, two under the cab, four in two rear tandem axles) with side skirts. Back: a sealed cargo pod, a rounded-box capsule with yellow hazard bands, armour ribs, a glowing magenta seal-door at the rear and neon strips. A small roof turret sits on the cab roof with twin barrels pointing forward. Everything is faceted and blocky; neon cyan and magenta trim lines glow along the edges, yellow-black hazard stripes mark the bumpers and pod. Wheels, skirts and underbody rest on the floor. The model is static.

parts.builds: Chassis and underbody: a long ladder frame slab from z=-3.9 to 3.9 with a dark underside, side skirts in hull with cyan neon strip lines and yellow-black hazard-striped small blocks, fuel and battery boxes, exhaust stacks behind the cab, mudguard arches above each wheel, and the front bumper with ram plate, bull bar, tow hooks and two lamp housings with lampWhite lights. Rear bumper with red tail lights and a hitch plate. Rivets and panel seam strips in hullDark.
parts.attaches: Top face at chassisTop height 1.3 carries the cab at cabFloor and the pod at podFloor; wheels attach at the axle mounts; the bumper reaches frontBumper.

parts.builds: Six large chunky low-poly wheels (radius 0.6, width 0.5; octagonal tyres in tyre colour, rim discs in rim with bolt rings and a glowing rimGlow hub), two at the front axle (z=2.8) and four on the rear tandem axles (z=-1.2 and z=-2.8), centred x=±1.2 with axle centres at y=0.6. Axle beams in metalDark between each wheel pair, with small suspension arms and shock absorbers reaching up to the chassis. Tyre tread blocks as small parts around each tyre.
parts.attaches: Axle lines at axleFront, axleRear1, axleRear2 (y=0.6); the lowest points of the tyres rest on y=0.

parts.builds: Wedge cab from z=1.2 to 3.6 sitting on cabFloor: hull body with a sloped hood, a big slanted glass visor in glass with cyan neon edge lines, side windows, angled armour plates in hullLight, door seams, mirrors on stalks, a roof light bar with magenta and cyan lamps, roof antenna with a tip glow, side vents, and a yellow-black hazard stripe band across the hood front. Faceted angular shapes, a small interior glimpse with a seat silhouette behind the visor.
parts.attaches: Rests on chassisTop at cabFloor; its roof at cabRoof carries the turret ring; its back wall meets the pod front at z=1.0.

parts.builds: Roof gun turret on turretRing (0,2.6,1.9): a ring base in hullDark, an octagonal faceted housing in gunmetal with hullLight armour plates, a sensor eye with a glowing cyan lens, twin barrels pointing forward (+Z) with muzzle brakes and ammo boxes on the sides, a belt feed, a small yellow hazard stripe and a magenta status light. Also a pair of searchlights flanking the cab roof at z=2.4 and a small radar dish on a stalk at the roof rear z=1.4.
parts.attaches: Sits on cabRoof/turretRing at y=2.6; nothing touches the floor.

parts.builds: The sealed cargo pod from z=-4.0 to 1.0 on podFloor: a rounded faceted capsule body in podShell with podShade lower half, heavy armour ribs every 0.8 m in hull, yellow-black hazard bands at both ends, bolted corner clamps strapping it to the chassis in metalDark with rivets, a rear circular seal-door in podSeal with a glowing magenta ring and lock bolts at podRear, cyan neon strips running along the top and sides, a small biohazard-style emblem and ID number blocks on the flanks, roof hatch, vent pipes and a top rail. Front face has pipe connectors toward the cab.
parts.attaches: Rests on chassisTop at podFloor; its front face meets the cab back wall at z=1.0; the seal-door sits at podRear.

calls.reasoning:
I'm planning a static cargo pod builder using parts with geometry and color, laying out dimensions for the pod's span, height, and width before placing components.

For the body, I'm working through an octagonal prism shape for the hull using a rotated cylinder with 8 segments, plus tapered end caps and a lower shading slab to suggest a chamfered rounded-box look without actual joints.

Still refining the octagon prism geometry...

Working out which half-cylinder corresponds to the upper shell after the rotation, tracking how the theta start and length need to shift to match the rotated vertex positions.

Testing offsets, I realize the octagon's flat-top vertices don't land on the horizontal midline, so splitting into clean upper/lower halves by segment count alone doesn't quite work—the equator cuts through mid-side rather than at vertices. This is getting fiddly enough that I should consider a simpler segmentation approach instead.

Simpler idea: abandon the prism-half approach and assemble the body from stacked boxes instead—a lower shading box and an upper shell box, each spanning the full width and depth but different y-ranges, so I can control the color transition cleanly without clipping issues.

Working out chamfer geometry...

I'll add shaded diamond cutouts to the lower box too, checking the vertex positions line up with the chassis floor, then move on to tapered end caps for the front and rear plates.

Now I'm planning the ribs spaced every 0.8m along the hull, with hazard bands near both ends. Each rib is built from a top plate, side plates, and rotated diagonal boxes forming a ring shape around the profile.

Working out the lower diamond rib placement similarly, mirroring the top-right logic for the bottom vertex, then consolidating the side plates into a single piece spanning y1.65–2.65 to cover both diamond vertices, plus adding a bottom rib box beneath the chassis.

Now I'm planning the hazard striping at both ends — using alternating black/yellow diagonal blocks along the top and sides to mimic warning tape, structured as a loop generating segments across x and y for each band position.

Still placing ribs, landing around 35 parts total. Now I'm designing the rear seal-door: an end plate, a cylindrical hatch with glow ring in magenta torus, plus a dark frame ring around it.

Adding lock bolts and spoke details...

Placing glow strips...

Now I'm adding small rivets on the clamp faces, then designing a biohazard-style emblem for the flank: a yellow disc with a dark ring and three small black discs around a center point, built from rotated cylinder discs stacked by radius.

Rearranging rib spacing to every 0.8 units and fitting the emblem into one of the gaps, then sketching a simple ID plate with small block digits as a placeholder detail near the side.

I'm also adding a roof hatch sized to fit between two ribs, positioning it in one of the open gaps along the roof.

Now I'm adding details: hatch border, crossing handle bars, and a small glowing status light, plus rear vent pipes with elbow caps and a thin top rail running along the roof edges.

I need to adjust the body length so pipe connectors fit within the z≤1 boundary: shrinking the pod body to end at z=0.8 and adding flange discs and short connector cylinders from 0.8 to 1.0 to meet the cab. I'm also repositioning the hazard band near z=0.6 to avoid overlapping the ribs.

Now I'm adding a front face plate panel at z≈0.83, side bolts, metal couplings with cyan glow collars, and working out a rear end plate frame with a door, making sure the door cylinder depth doesn't poke past the rear box boundary.

To avoid z-fighting I'm thinning the layers and spacing them slightly apart in depth: the plate sits between -3.98 and -3.95, the frame ring sits just behind it, and the door disc sits behind that, each with small depth offsets so they don't overlap exactly on the same face.

I'm also adding a magenta torus seal around the pod, dark spoke bars across the door, and a central hub cylinder with a glowing magenta core, positioning each with slight z-depth offsets so they read as distinct layered elements rather than clipping into each other.

Now I'm placing bolts at a ring radius just outside the torus, checking the hazard bumper and rear hazard bands are already covered, and considering a thin neon strip accent along the lower body line.

I'm working out where the diamond notch on the shade's side geometry intersects the mid box, tracing how the sloped edges between the vertices create a visible gap that the mid box needs to start lower to hide.

Then I tally up the parts needed: body pieces, diamonds, plates, and ribs with their diagonal and side segments.

Writing box and cylinder helpers...

Adding diagonal bracing geometry...

Still placing clamps and rivets...

For the emblem I'm layering concentric rings—black trim, yellow inner ring, then black dots at three angular positions around the center, using thin rotated cylinders as discs. Now I'm starting on the ID plate near the side, giving it a thin rectangular shape positioned at the lower section.

Still placing hull details...

Still placing vent caps and pipes...

Now I'm laying out the rear door geometry and the front face plate with its connector pipes and flanges positioned at symmetric offsets.

Placing those magenta neon strips on the mid box sides with length 4.6, then moving into the full build using glow effects and the trim/body/neon color palette I've defined.
